entities.summary: Carlo Mierendorff was a German politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPD) during the Weimar Republic. An intellectual activist and regional politician in the People's State of Hesse, he played a major role in the propaganda of the SPD and the anti-fascist Iron Front during the last years of the republic. He was elected to the Reichstag in 1930. After the Nazi rise to power, he was arrested and spent several years in concentration camps before being released in 1938. He then helped organise the underground resistance to the Nazi regime until his death in December 1943 in an Allied air raid on Leipzig.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in the SPD and regional politician in Hesse, Mierendorff played a key role in the propaganda of the party and the anti-fascist Iron Front during the Weimar Republic. He was arrested multiple times by the Nazis and spent several years in concentration camps before being released in 1938.
